static_traits.name: Chen Ruiqiu
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, sharing with an iguana
static_traits.social_status: Having a few close friends to confide in, but not yet discussing work-related shame with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; has not yet received psychotherapy or psychiatric treatment
static_traits.language_features: Slightly nervous but cooperative; clear expression; able to self-reflect; positive attitude; willing to try

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling ashamed and inferior because McDonald's work is seen as 'not real work'; although she enjoys it and finds it fun, this shame and not-good-enough feeling appears almost daily, especially when work comes up.
basic_info.core_demands: Because work-related shame and not-good-enough feelings affect overall mental health and self-esteem, hoping to improve these feelings through counseling.
growth_experiences: Starting McDonald's work about a year ago, initially feeling moderate stress, then shame and a sense of inadequacy gradually worsened due to societal stereotypes of the fast-food industry and others' reactions; especially obvious when talking about work with others, appearing almost daily.

At work had been thanked by customers and praised for a positive attitude; once during a busy shift obtained the manager's recognition of their effort; these positive moments made them briefly feel happy and valued, but were immediately covered by shame and negative self-evaluation.

special_situations.event: Being asked by others 'what work do you do?' or needing to introduce one's occupation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my work is not recognized by society, it means I am not successful; I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to avoid talking about work in social settings, reducing contact with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My work is not real work; I am not good enough

special_situations.event: Talking with friends or family about work, or seeing people around having high salaries and promotions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach their achievements, it equals failure; I am wasting potential
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding discussing work details, hiding or rarely talking about work-related information
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am wasting my potential; I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: Receiving thanks from customers or praise from managers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive feedback does not count; it cannot offset the low status of work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplaying or negating positive experiences; turning attention back to negative evaluations

special_situations.event: Thinking about society's stigma and contempt toward fast-food work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Social evaluation determines my personal worth
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on negative external information, ignoring one's own enjoyment of and sense of achievement from work
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Fast-food work is not worthy of respect

core_conflict.wish: Longs for respected and recognized self-worth, and to be seen for one's work contributions
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being looked down on, humiliated, negated (especially when work comes up)
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being evaluated by avoiding talking about work
Interpreting self-worth through self-deprecation and external standards, to temporarily relieve anxiety

object_relations.object_representation: Others / society with judgment and contempt

object_relations.self_representation: A self who works hard and longs to be seen

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others ask about his views on work and self-worth, or talk about the career achievements of people around him
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding others' attention or silence as potential judgment and contempt (transference: projecting the self-deprecating sense of worth onto others' gazes)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing unease gently and cautiously; using vague phrasing (e.g. 'maybe' / 'perhaps') to leave room; avoiding directly requesting support.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked to examine evidence and discuss positive resources and feedback at work
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding emphasis on the positive as ignoring the real social stigma; worrying about being seen as deluded or self-deceiving
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Explains mainly with objective data and social evaluation, reducing emotional expression, with a steady and comparatively calm tone.

manifestations: Viewing one's own work as 'not real work'; questioning its value and meaning
Overly cares about others' views and social evaluation, taking external standards as the basis of self-worth
outcomes: Increasing shame and sense of inadequacy
Decreased self-esteem and impaired sense of self-worth
Reduced motivation; fewer interest activities (soccer and video games)
Social avoidance; nervous discomfort when work comes up

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent harsh self-reproach (e.g. 'I am not successful / not good enough'); cautious speech when work topics come up
Worrying about others' views leading to unwillingness to discuss shame with friends

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains impulses to act toward other people or things, turning the energy originally meant to be sent outward onto themselves.
manifestations: Wanting to ask friends for help but choosing to 'endure it'; not talking about true feelings
Reduced socializing and interest activities; contracting energy inward to avoid external evaluation

exception_events.target_problem: When asked about work by others or after a busy shift, the client usually focuses on negative evaluations, feels ashamed and quickly negates positive feedback, leading to a decreased sense of self-worth.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During one busy shift, the manager recognized her effort on the spot and customers also expressed thanks; she felt happy and valued at the time, did not quickly belittle herself as usual, and her shame was markedly reduced.
exception_events.reason: Different support: receiving immediate positive feedback from the manager and customers; different approach: focusing on service in the moment, skills in play; different situation: tasks clear and busy, attention focused on contribution and value.

exception_events.target_problem: When work comes up in interactions with others, the client usually feels shame and inadequacy due to social stereotypes, and avoids further conversation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On one occasion a customer thanked her for her help and praised her positive attitude; at the time she experienced feeling seen and a sense of worth, and was more willing than usual to take in positive feedback.
exception_events.reason: Different support: customers' direct thanks and praise; different understanding: viewing the immediate service effect as a meaningful contribution; situational clue: concrete successful interactions on site strengthening inner affirmation.

positive_force: Has genuine love for and investment in the fast pace and customer interaction
Has received recognition from customers and the manager, able to experience a sense of being seen
Positive attitude; willing to try different perspectives and techniques (reality testing)
Has several close friends who can serve as potential support resources
negative_force: Self-worth excessively depends on external approval (External Validation)
Comparing and despair tendencies; often comparing with high earners and promoted people around
Negating positive experiences and mental filtering; continuously focusing on negative information
Shame and sense of self-inadequacy leading to social avoidance and decreased motivation; living habits affected

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding talking about work in social situations and reduced socializing
antecedent: Being asked about one's job or needing to introduce oneself
Discussing work with friends and family
Seeing people around get higher pay or promotions
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized society's stigma toward fast-food work, tying self-worth to external evaluation, producing cognitive biases of shame and self-deprecation
target_behavior.function: Escaping being evaluated and humiliated, gaining short-term safety and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships damaged; lowered self-esteem; decreased drive; fewer interest activities

target_behavior.behavior: Negating positive feedback; downplaying one's own achievements
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases (negating the positive, mental filtering) maintaining the negative core belief 'I am not good enough'
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a self-concept consistent with core beliefs, avoiding cognitive dissonance
target_behavior.consequence: Continuously declining sense of self-worth; low mood; work performance affected
